marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S7 and answer the following questions: Give the four-figure grid reference for ∆224.
common_errors: Candidates mentioned 'northing' prior to 'easting' number.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Provide regular practice regarding four-figure reference where easting number should be written before northing number. It should be left side easting and lower side northing.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S7 and answer the following questions: What is the contour interval used in the given map extract?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 20 metres
marking_schemes.model_answer: 20 metres
common_errors: Some candidates defined the term instead of mentioning the actual contour interval.
Unit was not mentioned by some candidates.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to mention 'unit'.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S7 and answer the following questions: Mention two man made features seen in grid square 2706.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Man made (2706) – lime kiln, covered tank, lined well, permanent hut/ hut/ settlement/ powerline/ powerline with poles/ chattri/ metalled road/ well. (Any two points)
key_points: Any one man-made feature from: lime kiln, covered tank, lined well, permanent hut/hut/settlement, powerline, powerline with poles, chattri, metalled road, well
Any second man-made feature from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two man-made features in grid square 2706 include a lime kiln and a lined well (any two from: lime kiln, covered tank, lined well, permanent hut/settlement, powerline, powerline with poles, chattri, metalled road, well).
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned 'overhead tank' but no symbol of overhead tank was found in this grid square.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Familiarise students with the 'index' given below the map and all symbols in the index.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S7 and answer the following questions: Mention two natural features seen in grid square 2905.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Natural (2905) – dry stream or stream/ seasonal stream/ sand dune/ sandy feature/ sand hill/ broken ground/ barren land/ plain. (Any two points)
key_points: Any one natural feature from: dry stream/stream, seasonal stream, sand dune, sandy feature, sand hill, broken ground, barren land, plain
Any second natural feature from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two natural features in grid square 2905 include a dry stream and a sand dune (any two from: dry stream/stream, seasonal stream, sand dune, sandy feature, sand hill, broken ground, barren land, plain).
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned 'trees' as a natural feature which is incorrect.
Some candidates wrote 'river' instead of 'stream'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain difference between 'River' and 'Stream' to differentiate them on the map.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S7 and answer the following questions: What do you understand by 1:50,000 printed below the map extract?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is Representative Fraction/RF/ type of scale/ scale in the form of ratio/ definition of RF/ it is universal scale.
key_points: It is a Representative Fraction (RF) / type of scale / scale in the form of ratio / universal scale — 1 unit on map equals 50,000 units on ground
marking_schemes.model_answer: 1:50,000 is the Representative Fraction (RF), a type of scale expressed as a ratio, meaning 1 unit on the map represents 50,000 units on the ground. It is a universal scale with no units.
accepted_alternatives: scale in the form of ratio
common_errors: Some candidates explained it in terms of 'units' which was incorrect as Representative Fraction does not have a unit.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to look at the 'pattern seen in the square' that is referred to rather than looking in 'wider adjacent area'.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S7 and answer the following questions: What is the pattern of drainage seen in the grid square 2505?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Dendritic
marking_schemes.model_answer: Dendritic
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned 'trellised' instead of 'dendritic'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Diagrams may be used to explain different types of drainage patterns.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S7 and answer the following questions: What do you understand by .10r in 2709?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is the relative height of sand dune which is 10 metres.
key_points: It is the relative height of the sand dune
The relative height is 10 metres (in relation to the surrounding area, not sea level)
marking_schemes.model_answer: The .10r in 2709 denotes the relative height of a sand dune, which is 10 metres above the surrounding area (not above mean sea level).
common_errors: Some candidates did not write the correct term 'Relative Height'.
Some candidates incorrectly mentioned '10 metres above mean sea level'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students that any number with small 'r' depicts 'relative height' which is in relation to the 'surrounding area' and not 'sea level'. Familiarize students with terms – 'Height', 'Relative Height', and 'Altitude'.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S7 and answer the following questions: What is the compass direction of Mahudi Nani (2604) from Panswala (2909)?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Southwest/ SW
marking_schemes.model_answer: Southwest / SW
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss '8 cardinal points of the compass'.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the extract of the Survey of India Map Sheet No. G43S7 and answer the following questions: Calculate the area in kilometre square of the region enclosed between Easting 26 to 29 and Northing 05 to 11.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Area = Length × Breadth = Scale of the given map is 2 cm to 1 km. = 3 x 6 = 18 grid square. Area of 1 grid square = 1 km2. ∴ 18 km2
key_points: Correct method: Area = Length × Breadth using map scale (2 cm to 1 km)
Number of grid squares = 3 × 6 = 18
Area of 1 grid square = 1 km2, therefore total area = 18 km2
marking_schemes.model_answer: Using the map scale of 2 cm to 1 km, the region spans 3 eastings and 6 northings, giving 18 grid squares. Since each grid square equals 1 km², the total area is 18 km².
common_errors: Some candidates did not calculate the answer correctly.
Other candidates failed to mention the 'unit' (km²).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Enable students to do 'simple calculation of area' by using 'scale of the map'. Encourage students to mention the 'unit' after the answer.
marking_schemes.topic: Map Study: Interpretation of Topological Maps

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label the Satpura.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Satpura marked and labelled correctly between Narmada and Tapi rivers.
key_points: Satpura range marked correctly between Narmada and Tapi (Tapti) rivers, parallel to them without touching either river
Correctly labelled
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark the Satpura range between the Narmada and Tapi rivers, running parallel to them without touching either river, and label it 'Satpura'.
common_errors: Some candidates made a line too broad, and it touched the rivers on both sides or one side.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Mark Satpura between Narmada and Tapi (Tapti) and not touch the river (should be made parallel).

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Shade and label the Gulf of Kutch.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Gulf of Kutch shaded and labelled correctly.
key_points: Gulf of Kutch shaded correctly (northwestern coast of India, north of Kathiawar peninsula)
Correctly labelled 'Gulf of Kutch'
marking_schemes.model_answer: Shade the Gulf of Kutch on the northwestern coast of India, north of the Kathiawar (Saurashtra) peninsula, and label it 'Gulf of Kutch'.
common_errors: Several candidates marked the area of 'Gulf of Khambat' instead of 'Gulf of Kutch'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Provide regular practice of map work and emphasize use of arrows and shading for marking the Gulfs and Bays.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label the River Chambal.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — River Chambal marked and labelled correctly.
key_points: River Chambal marked correctly (flows through Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan, tributary of Yamuna)
Arrow pointing in correct direction of flow, labelled 'Chambal'
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark River Chambal flowing through Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan into the Yamuna, with an arrow pointing in the correct direction of flow, and label it 'Chambal'.
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned 'Chambal' between the rivers without the use of an arrow pointing towards the right direction.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Show arrows to point towards the correct answer. Guide students to shade/highlight the river using blue colour.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label Delhi.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Delhi marked and labelled correctly on the right bank of Yamuna.
key_points: Delhi marked correctly on the right bank of Yamuna river
Correctly labelled 'Delhi'
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark Delhi on the right bank of the Yamuna river with a dot touching the river, and label it 'Delhi'.
common_errors: Some candidates made a very large dot and marked it on the left bank of Yamuna.
In some cases, candidates made dot away from Yamuna.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Delhi is on the right bank of Yamuna and so the dot should be made touching the river.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label 80°30' E longitude.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — 82°30'E longitude marked and labelled correctly.
key_points: 80°30'E longitude marked correctly as a vertical line
Correctly labelled '80°30'E'
marking_schemes.model_answer: Draw a vertical line at 80°30'E longitude running from north to south across India and label it '80°30'E'.
common_errors: Few candidates marked 'Tropic of Cancer' instead of the longitude.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify the difference between 'latitude and longitude'.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label Jharia coalfield.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Jharia coalfield marked and labelled correctly between the fork of river Damodar.
key_points: Jharia coalfield marked correctly between the fork of river Damodar in Jharkhand
Correctly labelled 'Jharia'
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark Jharia coalfield between the fork of river Damodar in Jharkhand and label it 'Jharia'.
common_errors: A very large area was marked by some candidates.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: 'Jharia' should be marked 'between the fork' of river 'Damodar'.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Mark with arrows and name the Southwest Monsoon winds.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Southwest Monsoon winds marked with arrows in correct direction from sea towards land, labelled correctly.
key_points: Arrows drawn in water body pointing towards land in the correct southwest-to-northeast direction
Labelled 'SW Monsoon Wind' or equivalent
marking_schemes.model_answer: Draw arrows in the water body (Arabian Sea/Bay of Bengal) pointing towards the land in the southwest direction and label them 'SW Monsoon Wind'.
common_errors: Some candidates missed making arrowheads.
Few candidates made the arrows in incorrect direction.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Arrows should be 'made in water body' pointing 'towards the land' and label it.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Mark and label the Karakoram Pass.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Karakoram Pass marked and labelled correctly in the northern Karakoram range (Ladakh region).
key_points: Karakoram Pass marked correctly in the Karakoram range in the far north (Ladakh/J&K region)
Correctly labelled 'Karakoram Pass'
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mark the Karakoram Pass in the Karakoram range in the far north of India (Ladakh region) and label it 'Karakoram Pass'.
common_errors: Some candidates incorrectly marked 'Nathu La' or made the pass towards the westward direction.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Provide clarity in directions like East, West, North, or South to the student. Advise students to read the question properly.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Shade and label a sparsely populated region in Western India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Sparsely populated region in Western India (e.g., Rajasthan/Thar Desert region) shaded and labelled correctly.
key_points: Sparsely populated region shaded correctly in western India (e.g., Thar Desert/Rajasthan)
Correctly labelled 'Sparse Population' or equivalent
marking_schemes.model_answer: Shade the Thar Desert region in western India (Rajasthan) and label it 'Sparse Population' or 'Sparsely Populated Region'.
common_errors: Some candidates did not label the shaded area.
Some candidates marked the sparsely populated region on the eastern side rather than the western side.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to do the labelling after marking/shading the required area. Provide clarity in directions.

marking_schemes.question_text: On the outline map of India provided: Shade an area having Alluvial soil.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Refer to marking scheme map — Alluvial soil area shaded correctly (Indo-Gangetic plain / river delta regions), labelled 'Alluvial Soil'.
key_points: Alluvial soil area shaded correctly — Indo-Gangetic plains or major river delta regions within India
Correctly labelled 'Alluvial Soil'
marking_schemes.model_answer: Shade the Indo-Gangetic plain (northern plains of India) as an area of alluvial soil and label it 'Alluvial Soil'.
common_errors: Some candidates either missed labelling or shaded the areas of Nepal which was incorrect.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to do shading only in 'Indian' area and not in the 'neighbouring countries'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the correct answer: Which of the following area receives rain from the North East Monsoon? (a) Konkan coast (b) Ganga basin (c) Coromandel coast (d) Malabar coast
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (c) Coromandel coast
marking_schemes.model_answer: (c) Coromandel coast
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned 'Malabar coast' rather than 'Coromandel coast'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Work on the conceptual clarity of the topic 'climate' and ensure students know the difference between S.W. Monsoon and N.E. Monsoon.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the correct answer: Which is the most widespread soil of India? (a) Red soil (b) Alluvial soil (c) Laterite soil (d) Black soil
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (b) Alluvial soil
marking_schemes.model_answer: (b) Alluvial soil
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to read the question and options given therein properly to answer the question correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the correct answer: Which type of forest is found mostly in the coastal areas of India? (a) Tropical Evergreen Forest (b) Tropical Desert Forest (c) Littoral Forest (d) Tropical Deciduous Forest
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (c) Littoral forest
marking_schemes.model_answer: (c) Littoral forest
common_errors: Some candidates missed reading 'mostly', thus mentioned 'Tropical Evergreen' instead of 'Littoral'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to read the question and options given therein properly to answer the question correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the correct answer: Which of the following is a ground water source? (a) Pond (b) Lake (c) Spring (d) River
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (c) Spring
marking_schemes.model_answer: (c) Spring
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned 'Pond' as a ground water source.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Familiarize students with the terms 'ground water' and 'surface water' with examples.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the correct answer: Copper is alloyed with Zinc to form: (a) Stainless steel (b) Brass (c) Bronze (d) Aluminium
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (b) Brass
marking_schemes.model_answer: (b) Brass
common_errors: Candidates were confused between 'brass and bronze'.
Some candidates mentioned 'aluminium'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clarify uses of the minerals.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the correct answer: Hirakud dam is based on which of the following rivers? (a) River Godavari (b) River Mahanadi (c) River Krishna (d) River Narmada
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (b) Mahanadi
marking_schemes.model_answer: (b) Mahanadi
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned 'Narmada' which was incorrect.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Familiarize with the 'rivers on which the dams' are made.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the correct answer: Which of the following is NOT a problem of Indian agriculture? (a) Dependence on monsoon (b) Small land holdings (c) Two main cropping seasons (d) Use of traditional methods of farming
options: (d) Use of traditional methods of farming
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (vii) (b) Two main cropping seasons
marking_schemes.model_answer: (c) Two main cropping seasons
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned the 'unique feature of Indian agriculture' as response instead of the 'problem' which the question demanded.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to read the question and options given therein properly to answer the question correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the correct answer: Which of the following is a basic / key industry? (a) Iron and Steel Industry (b) Silk Industry (c) Electronic Industry (d) Cotton textile Industry
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (viii) (a) Iron and steel
marking_schemes.model_answer: (a) Iron and Steel Industry
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned 'cotton textile' indicating lack of clarity on the term 'key industry'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Students must know the meaning of a 'basic' or 'key industry'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the correct answer: Which of the following is a staple food grain of Indians? (a) Wheat (b) Rice (c) Gram (d) Arhar
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (ix) (b) Rice/ wheat
marking_schemes.model_answer: (b) Rice / wheat
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Focus on the concept 'Staple grain of Indians'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Choose the correct answer: Which of the following method of waste disposal is harmful? (a) Composting (b) Segregation (c) Dumping (d) Vermicomposting
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (x) (c) Dumping
marking_schemes.model_answer: (c) Dumping
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned 'Vermicomposting' reflecting lack of clarity on the concept.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Build clarity of concept related to method of waste disposal and vermicomposting etc.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the seasons of India and mention the duration of each season.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Summer – hot & dry season/ hot season/ hot weather season. Rainy – hot and wet season/ SW monsoon season/ advancing monsoon season/ onset of monsoon/ monsoon. Retreating monsoon. Winter – cold & dry season/ NE monsoon season/ cold season/ cold weather season.
key_points: Summer / Hot and dry season (March–May)
Rainy / SW Monsoon season / hot and wet season (June–September)
Retreating Monsoon season (October–November)
Winter / Cold and dry season / NE Monsoon season (December–February)
marking_schemes.model_answer: India has four seasons: Summer (hot and dry season, March–May), Rainy/SW Monsoon season (hot and wet, June–September), Retreating Monsoon (October–November), and Winter/cold and dry season (December–February).
common_errors: Many candidates' responses lacked the technical terms expected in the answer.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to use technical terms relating to the seasons such as – hot and dry season, hot and wet season, retreating monsoon season, cold and dry season.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why maximum rainfall in India occurs after the summer season?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: During summer low pressure is created over land. This attracts the wind from sea leading to rain.
key_points: During summer, low pressure is created over land due to high temperatures
This attracts moisture-laden winds from the sea, leading to heavy rainfall
marking_schemes.model_answer: During summer, intense heating of the land creates a low pressure zone over India. This low pressure attracts moisture-laden winds from the sea, which bring heavy rainfall when they rise over the land.
common_errors: Candidates were not able to explain the relation of high heat during summer leading to low pressure conditions on land which in turn attracts the rain-bearing winds.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain and discuss with students the basic concepts related to climate such as concept of 'low pressure' and 'high pressure'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: The Malabar coast receives heavy rainfall in the month of July but the Coromandel coast during this time remains comparatively dry.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Coromandel coast is in Tamil Nadu which lies in the rain shadow region of Arabian sea branch and the Bay of Bengal branch blows parallel to the coast.
key_points: The Coromandel coast lies in the rain shadow region of the Arabian Sea branch of the SW Monsoon
The Bay of Bengal branch of the SW Monsoon blows parallel to the Coromandel coast and does not cause rainfall
marking_schemes.model_answer: The Malabar coast receives heavy rainfall in July because it directly faces the Arabian Sea branch of the SW Monsoon. The Coromandel coast, however, lies in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats (for the Arabian Sea branch), and the Bay of Bengal branch blows parallel to the coast, so it receives little rainfall during this period.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: 'Relief rainfall' should be explained using diagrams and examples from India.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: Punjab receives rainfall in winter season.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Punjab receives rainfall in winter due to the Western disturbance/ temperate cyclone/ Westerly depression.
key_points: Punjab receives winter rainfall due to Western Disturbances / temperate cyclones / Westerly depressions originating in the Mediterranean region
marking_schemes.model_answer: Punjab receives rainfall in winter due to Western Disturbances — temperate cyclones originating in the Mediterranean region that travel eastward and bring rainfall to northwestern India.
common_errors: In some cases, candidates mentioned 'source as NE Monsoon' which was an incorrect response.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain and discuss with students the basic concepts related to climate.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: Mumbai is warmer than Delhi in the month of December.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Mumbai lies near the coast so gets influence by the sea and experiences a moderate climate whereas Delhi has continental location and has extreme temperature conditions resulting in high annual range of temperature.
key_points: Mumbai is near the coast and is moderated by the sea, experiencing a moderate climate in December
Delhi has a continental location, far from the sea, and experiences extreme cold in December
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mumbai is warmer than Delhi in December because Mumbai is located on the coast and is moderated by the Arabian Sea, keeping temperatures mild. Delhi, with its inland/continental location, experiences extreme cold in winter due to the absence of the moderating influence of the sea.
common_errors: In some cases, candidates mentioned 'nearness to Equator' rather than 'distance from sea'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to provide detailed explanations for both cities when the question mentions two cities.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the climate data of Station X (Jan–Dec temperature and rainfall) and answer: Calculate the annual range of temperature of Station X. [Temperature data: Jan 21.0, Feb 21.9, Mar 24.3, Apr 27.2, May 28.0, Jun 26.4, Jul 26.1, Aug 25.4, Sep 26.0, Oct 26.0, Nov 23.8, Dec 21.2 °C]
key_points: Annual range of temperature = Maximum temperature – Minimum temperature = 28°C – 21°C = 7°C
marking_schemes.model_answer: The annual range of temperature of Station X is 28°C − 21°C = 7°C.
common_errors: In some cases, candidates failed to mention the 'units'.
Calculation errors were found in certain cases.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Lay emphasis on writing of 'unit' in the calculation related questions.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the climate data of Station X (Jan–Dec temperature and rainfall) and answer: Name the wind that brings most of the rainfall to this station. [Rainfall data shows peak in Oct–Nov: Oct 31.6 cm, Nov 34.5 cm]
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Retreating monsoon winds/ NE monsoon
marking_schemes.model_answer: Retreating monsoon winds / NE monsoon
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Regularly provide practice of application-based questions on climate data.

marking_schemes.question_text: Study the climate data of Station X (Jan–Dec temperature and rainfall) and answer: On which coast of India is Station X located? [Rainfall peaks in Oct–Nov suggesting NE monsoon dominance]
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Eastern coast / SE coast / Coromandel coast
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Eastern coast/ SE coast/ coromandel coast
marking_schemes.model_answer: Eastern coast / SE coast / Coromandel coast
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned 'city instead of coast'.
Few candidates were not able to identify the coastal area.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to read the question carefully and answer accordingly. Discuss the difference between region/coast/place.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention any two causes of soil erosion in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Deforestation, Overgrazing, Faulty farming techniques, urbanisation, industrialisation, lack of vegetation cover, floods, heavy rain, mining, construction of dam, excessive use of chemicals.
key_points: Any one cause from: deforestation, overgrazing, faulty farming techniques, urbanisation, industrialisation, lack of vegetation cover, floods, heavy rain, mining, construction of dam, excessive use of chemicals
Any second cause from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two causes of soil erosion in India are deforestation (removal of trees exposes soil to wind and water) and overgrazing (animals strip vegetation, leaving soil bare and vulnerable).
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned 'agents of soil erosion' in place of 'causes'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Share with students the difference between the causes and the agents of soil erosion.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name two soil conservation methods that may be practised in arid (dry) regions.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Planting of shelter belts, strip cropping, afforestation or wind breakers.
key_points: Any one method from: planting of shelter belts, strip cropping, afforestation, wind breakers
Any second method from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two soil conservation methods suitable for arid regions are planting of shelter belts (rows of trees to reduce wind erosion) and afforestation/wind breakers to protect soil from wind.
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned conservation methods in general instead of methods specific to arid areas.
Some candidates did not understand the meaning of 'arid'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Make clear to students the conservation methods specific for humid and dry areas and the right words to describe them.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two characteristics of Black soil.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Sticky when wet, cracks when dry, moisture retentive, black in colour. Colour varies from black to chestnut brown, self-ploughing capacity, fine grained, clayey in texture, rich in LIMCAP, poor in nitrogen, organic matter & phosphorus.
key_points: Any one characteristic from: sticky when wet, cracks when dry, moisture retentive, black in colour (varies from black to chestnut brown), self-ploughing capacity, fine grained, clayey in texture, rich in lime/iron/magnesium/calcium/aluminium/potassium (LIMCAP), poor in nitrogen/organic matter/phosphorus
Any second distinct characteristic from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Black soil is sticky when wet and develops deep cracks when dry (self-ploughing capacity). It is fine-grained and clayey in texture, highly moisture retentive, rich in lime, iron, magnesium, calcium, and potassium, but poor in nitrogen, organic matter, and phosphorus.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss composition/characteristics of each type of soil as per the scope of syllabus.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the soil that is found on the summits of Eastern and Western Ghats.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (a) Laterite soil
marking_schemes.model_answer: Laterite soil
common_errors: Candidates were found to be confused related to Red soil / Black soil.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Focus on characteristics of soil with reference to other types of soil to enable students to bring out the difference between each type.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the soil that is suitable for dry farming.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (b) Red soil/ Black soil
marking_schemes.model_answer: Red soil / Black soil
common_errors: Some confusion with 'Laterite soil' was found.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explanation regarding formation of each type of soil must be done using a map to show the area in which the soil has developed.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the soil that varies in texture.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (c) Alluvial soil
marking_schemes.model_answer: Alluvial soil
common_errors: Candidates were not clear on the meaning of 'texture'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Certain terms such as texture, soil profile, soil conservation etc. must be discussed in class.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: Terrace farming is an ideal soil conservation method for hilly areas.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Terrace farming prevents soil erosion by slowing the speed of running water and thus contributes to soil conservation.
key_points: Terrace farming slows the speed of running water on steep slopes, thereby preventing soil erosion
marking_schemes.model_answer: Terrace farming cuts hilly slopes into level steps, which slows the speed of running water and reduces its erosive force, thereby preventing soil erosion and conserving soil.
common_errors: Candidates were unable to explain the 'steep slope with speed of running water' and 'soil erosion'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: More concept building is required. Explain 'Khadar and Bhangar difference using map of India' for better clarity of the concept.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: Khadar soils are preferred over Bhangar soils.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Khadar soils is more fertile than Bhangar soils. Khadar is new alluvium, fine grained. Does not have calcite modules. Replenished.
key_points: Khadar is new alluvium — finer grained, more fertile, and regularly replenished by flood deposits
Bhangar is old alluvium with calcite nodules (kankars), less fertile and not replenished
marking_schemes.model_answer: Khadar soils are preferred because they are new alluvium — finer grained, more fertile, and regularly replenished by annual floods. Bhangar soils are older alluvium with calcite nodules and are less fertile.
common_errors: Some candidates were unable to explain the Khadar and Bhangar difference.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain 'Khadar and Bhangar difference using map of India' for better clarity of the concept.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a geographical reason for the following: Foothills of Himalayas have been affected by soil erosion.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Due to large scale deforestation in past/ heavy rain/ torrential downpour
key_points: Large-scale deforestation has removed vegetation cover, exposing soil
Heavy/torrential rainfall in the Himalayan foothills washes away the unprotected soil
marking_schemes.model_answer: The foothills of the Himalayas have been affected by soil erosion due to large-scale deforestation and torrential rainfall. The removal of forest cover exposes the soil, which is then washed away by heavy rains.
common_errors: Candidates were not able to describe 'deforestation' / 'heavy rainfall' leading to 'soil erosion'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Share reasons for 'soil erosion in different areas of India' and focus on concept building.

marking_schemes.question_text: State two ways in which forests help in protecting the environment.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Moderates the climate, controls humidity, temperature, and precipitation, plays a major role in carbon cycle, absorbs carbon di-oxide, maintain purity of air, controls atmospheric pollution, controls soil erosion, Controls flood, Helps to increase underground water table, helps in percolation, provides humus to soil and increases the fertility, regulates water cycle, reduces the impact of global warming. (Any two points)
key_points: Any one environmental benefit from: moderates climate, controls humidity/temperature/precipitation, absorbs CO2/carbon cycle, maintains air purity, controls atmospheric pollution, controls soil erosion, controls floods, increases underground water table, helps percolation, provides humus/increases soil fertility, regulates water cycle, reduces global warming impact
Any second distinct environmental benefit from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Forests help protect the environment by absorbing carbon dioxide and maintaining the purity of air, thereby reducing atmospheric pollution and the impact of global warming. They also control soil erosion, regulate the water cycle, and help increase underground water table through percolation.
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned the importance of forest not in context of/related to the environment.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Share importance/benefits of forest for both economic and environmental aspects.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two ways in which Tropical Desert vegetation has adapted to its environment.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Xerophytic, leaves modified to thorns, long roots, thick stem, symbiotic relation with stinging ants/ very small leaves/ waxy leaves/ thick leaves/ rolled up leaves/ sunken stomata/ succulent plant/ drought tolerant/ thick stem/ woody stem. (Any two points)
key_points: Any one adaptation from: xerophytic nature, leaves modified to thorns, long roots to reach deep water, thick stem to store water, very small/waxy/thick/rolled-up leaves, sunken stomata, succulent/drought tolerant, woody stem, symbiotic relation with stinging ants
Any second distinct adaptation from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tropical desert vegetation has adapted by modifying leaves into thorns to reduce water loss through transpiration, and by developing long roots to access deep underground water sources. Plants also have thick, succulent stems to store water and may have waxy or sunken stomata to minimise water loss.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain, using map of annual rainfall, soil distribution and temperature condition, the growth and the characteristics of vegetation belts of India.

marking_schemes.question_text: In which natural vegetation belt is Sundari tree found?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (a) Littoral/ Tidal forests/ mangrove
marking_schemes.model_answer: Littoral / Tidal forests / Mangrove
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned 'Sundarbans' instead of the name of natural vegetation belt (Littoral).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to learn the names of important trees that grow in the 'natural vegetation belts of India'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is the Tropical Deciduous Forest commercially the most exploited forest belt of India? (Two points)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: sparsely located/scattered-easy to cut/exploit, hard wood-durable, high value of timber, provides fruits and other forest products, easily accessible, easy to transport. (Any two points)
key_points: Any one reason from: trees are sparsely located/scattered so easy to cut and exploit, hardwood that is durable, high value of timber, provides fruits and other forest products, easily accessible, easy to transport
Any second distinct reason from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tropical Deciduous Forest is the most commercially exploited because the trees are sparsely located/scattered, making them easy to access and cut. The forests yield valuable hardwood that is durable and commands a high timber value, and the relatively flat terrain makes transportation of timber easy.
accepted_alternatives: Provides fruits and other forest products
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Revise the characteristics of each natural vegetation belt.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name one region in India where Tropical Evergreen Forest is found.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Western side of Western Ghats / NE hills / Andaman & Nicobar / Western Maharashtra / Western Karnataka / Kerala / Lakshadweep
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Tropical Evergreen Forest is found on the western side of Western Ghats/ western slopes of Western ghats/ windward side of Western ghats/ NE hills/ submountain of West Bengal/ Andaman & Nicobar/ Lakshadweep. Western Maharashtra, Western Karnataka, Kerala, Western Ghats.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tropical Evergreen Forest is found on the western slopes (windward side) of the Western Ghats.
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned the 'names of the states' instead of 'region'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain to students that when the question demands 'region' then merely 'names of the states' is not sufficient.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention the temperature and rainfall conditions found suitable for the growth of Tropical Evergreen Forest.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Temperature – 25°C–27°C (15–30°C), Rainfall – more than 200 cms.
key_points: Temperature: 25°C–27°C (acceptable range: 15–30°C)
Rainfall: more than 200 cm annually
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tropical Evergreen Forests require a high temperature of 25°C–27°C (range 15–30°C) and very heavy annual rainfall of more than 200 cm.
common_errors: Some candidates were found confused with the 'temperature and rainfall' and provided incorrect answers.
A number of candidates mentioned 'characteristics' rather than 'climatic conditions'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Provide regular practice to ensure learning the temperature and rainfall conditions. Provide clarity to students regarding appropriate places to mention climatic conditions and its characteristics.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Agriculture sector in India needs the support of irrigation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: India experiences a tropical monsoon type of climate, Rainfall is seasonal/ erratic/ unreliable/ irregular/ uncertain/ unevenly distributed/ sporadic. The country has a very long growing season if water for the crop is ensured. Some crops like rice & sugarcane need more water for higher productivity of crops.
key_points: Indian rainfall is seasonal, erratic, unreliable, irregular, uncertain, unevenly distributed — crops cannot depend on it alone
A long growing season is possible if water is ensured through irrigation; water-intensive crops like rice and sugarcane need more water than rainfall alone can provide
marking_schemes.model_answer: India has a tropical monsoon climate where rainfall is seasonal, erratic, and unevenly distributed, making agriculture dependent on monsoons unreliable. Irrigation ensures a steady water supply throughout the long growing season and meets the higher water requirements of crops like rice and sugarcane.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Provide more practice of reasoning-based questions. Explain the 'type of terrain' necessary for the development of various means of irrigation.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give a reason for the following: Well irrigation is a popular means of irrigation in Northern India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Well, is simplest & cheapest source. It is an independent source/ soft soil/ high water table. Well can be dug at any convenient place. Several chemicals are mixed in the Well/ Well need small area.
key_points: Wells are the simplest and cheapest source of irrigation; they are independent and can be dug at any convenient place
Northern India has soft soil (alluvial plains) and a high water table, making well-digging easy and effective
marking_schemes.model_answer: Well irrigation is popular in Northern India because the alluvial plains have soft soil and a high water table, making it easy and inexpensive to dig wells. Wells are also an independent source of irrigation that can be dug at any convenient location near the field.
accepted_alternatives: Can be dug at any convenient place
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the 'methods of irrigation' and its 'distribution' using a map.

marking_schemes.question_text: Distinguish between Inundation canal and Perennial canal.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Inundation Canal: taken out from rivers without any regulating systems like weir and barrages; canals are taken out when rivers are in flood and there is excess water; only lower-level regions can be irrigated. Perennial Canal: useful throughout the year as they draw water from perennial rivers/artificial lakes; serve throughout the year; supply water during hot/dry season enabling cultivation round the year.
key_points: Inundation canal: taken from rivers without regulators (no weir/barrage); functional only during floods; irrigates only lower-level regions
Perennial canal: drawn from perennial rivers/artificial lakes; functional throughout the year; supplies water even in hot/dry seasons enabling year-round cultivation
marking_schemes.model_answer: Inundation canals are taken from rivers without any regulating structures (weirs or barrages) and function only when the river is in flood, irrigating only low-lying areas. Perennial canals draw water from perennial rivers or artificial lakes through regulated structures and supply water throughout the year, including the dry season, enabling year-round cultivation.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss and explain 'two types of canals', its 'source' along with their 'merits and demerits' of both kinds of canals.

marking_schemes.question_text: Where in India is Tank irrigation most widely used?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Deccan plateau / Peninsular area / Peninsular plateau (Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Telangana)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Tank irrigation is prevalent in Deccan plateau/ Peninsular area/ Peninsular plateau widely used in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra/Karnataka, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan/ Uttar Pradesh/ Telangana
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tank irrigation is most widely used in the Deccan plateau / Peninsular India.
common_errors: 'Peninsular region of India / southern region' was the expected answer but some candidates mentioned names of states.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Make students aware of the linked/connected question — if the answer of the first goes wrong then the second is automatically considered incorrect.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one factor that has led to the popularity of tank irrigation in the Peninsular/Deccan plateau region.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: The rainwater is collected in natural pits and depressions which are easily available in peninsular. These regions are made of hard rock/ impermeable rock. Seasonal rivers/ seasonal rain (Any one point)
key_points: Any one factor from: natural pits and depressions easily available in Peninsular India; hard/impermeable rock prevents percolation so water collects; seasonal rivers/seasonal rain make stored tank water necessary
marking_schemes.model_answer: The Peninsular plateau is made of hard, impermeable rock that prevents water from percolating, allowing it to collect in natural pits and depressions, making tank irrigation practical and popular.
accepted_alternatives: Natural pits and depressions easily available
common_errors: It was a linked question, so if the first answer was wrong, then the second was automatically considered incorrect.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Make students aware of the linked/connected question.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention one advantage of using tank as a means of irrigation.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Rainwater can be easily collected in more quantity. Tank irrigation is cheaper than other type of irrigation as the rainwater is collected in natural pits and depressions. As the water is collected and used in dry season, it uses the water table of the surrounding region. Operation in hands of farmer help in water conservation. (Any one point)
key_points: Any one advantage from: rainwater easily collected in quantity; cheaper than other irrigation types; water available in dry season; operation in hands of farmer aids water conservation
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tank irrigation is cheaper than other methods as it uses naturally occurring pits and depressions to collect rainwater, requiring minimal investment, and makes water available to farmers during the dry season.
accepted_alternatives: Rainwater can be easily collected in more quantity
Operation in hands of farmer — helps water conservation
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Do a comparative study with the help of flow chart or table for 'different means of irrigation' with the advantages and disadvantages of each.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is Rainwater Harvesting?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It means capturing rain where it falls or capturing the runoff in your own village or town. And taking measures to keep that water clean by not allowing polluting activities to take place in the catchment.
key_points: Capturing rain where it falls or capturing runoff in the local area
Taking measures to keep the collected water clean by preventing polluting activities in the catchment
marking_schemes.model_answer: Rainwater harvesting means capturing rain where it falls or collecting runoff in one's village or town, and taking measures to keep that water clean by preventing polluting activities in the catchment area.
common_errors: Many candidates provided a very general answer such as 'it is collection of rainwater'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to mention correct definitions using key words.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give two ways in which Rainwater Harvesting is important for India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Helps replenish water levels, Provide drinking water, Provide irrigation water, Increase groundwater recharge, Reduce soil erosion, Reduce flooding, Reduce pollution from chemicals of surface and ground water, Independent water supply, Prevents surface runoff. (Any two points)
key_points: Any one benefit from: replenishes water levels/groundwater recharge, provides drinking water, provides irrigation water, reduces soil erosion, reduces flooding, reduces surface/groundwater pollution, provides independent water supply, prevents surface runoff
Any second distinct benefit from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Rainwater harvesting is important for India because it helps replenish groundwater levels and provides an independent source of drinking and irrigation water. It also reduces surface runoff, thereby minimising soil erosion and flooding.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain 'water crisis faced by India' and the 'remedies' for the same.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the state of India that leads in the production of Manganese.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (a) Madhya Pradesh is the largest producer of Manganese in the country.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Madhya Pradesh
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Revisit and share 'mining areas/states for the minerals'.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is the importance of Manganese for the Iron and Steel industry?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Used in Iron & Steel industry It makes the Steel tough & rust proof/ increases strength of steel
key_points: Manganese makes steel tough, rust-proof, and increases the strength of steel in the Iron and Steel industry
marking_schemes.model_answer: Manganese is used in the Iron and Steel industry because it makes steel tough, rust-proof, and increases its overall strength and durability.
accepted_alternatives: Makes steel tough and rust proof
common_errors: Majority of candidates did not pay attention to the question and mentioned general importance of 'manganese' instead of relating it to 'Iron and steel'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to mention the 'uses of minerals' in tabular form to make learning easier.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is conventional source of energy not considered an eco-friendly source of energy?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Most of the resources cause pollution (Burning of Coal). They might get exhausted very soon in future/ non-renewable. Large scale pollution is caused at the site of mining and place of use. Carbon emission/ global warming/ air pollution. Pressure on resources. Releases poisonous gases. Excessive mining leads to ecological disbalance. Dust pollution. (Any two points)
key_points: Any one reason from: burning causes air pollution/carbon emissions/global warming; they are non-renewable and may get exhausted; large-scale pollution at mining sites; releases poisonous gases; excessive mining leads to ecological imbalance; dust pollution
Any second distinct reason from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Conventional sources of energy such as coal and petroleum are not eco-friendly because burning them releases carbon dioxide and other poisonous gases, causing air pollution and global warming. They are also non-renewable resources that will eventually be exhausted, and their mining causes large-scale environmental pollution and ecological imbalance.
accepted_alternatives: Excessive mining leads to ecological imbalance
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss and revisit the advantages and disadvantages of conventional source of energy.

marking_schemes.question_text: How is Bhakra Nangal dam beneficial for Punjab?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It provides cheap hydel power, helps in irrigation and soil conservation, control floods, recreation/ tourist/ attraction.
key_points: Any one benefit from: provides cheap hydel power; helps in irrigation and soil conservation; controls floods; provides recreation/tourism attraction
marking_schemes.model_answer: The Bhakra Nangal dam benefits Punjab by providing cheap hydroelectric power, supporting irrigation across large agricultural areas, controlling floods, and conserving soil.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the benefits of multipurpose dams. Make students aware of the names of states benefitted by the projects.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name two states where coal is mined in abundance.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, Odisha (any two)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, Odisha (Any two)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh (any two from: Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, West Bengal, Odisha).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Revisit and share 'mining areas/states for the minerals'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention one advantage of using wind energy.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is ecofriendly and renewable, reduces pressure on conventional sources, clean, sustainable, cost effective, no greenhouse gases (Any one)
key_points: Any one advantage from: eco-friendly and renewable, reduces pressure on conventional sources, clean, sustainable, cost effective, produces no greenhouse gases
marking_schemes.model_answer: Wind energy is eco-friendly and renewable — it produces no greenhouse gases or pollution, is sustainable, and helps reduce dependence on conventional fossil fuel sources.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss advantages of non-conventional energy sources.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name a mineral used to generate nuclear energy.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Uranium / Thorium / Beryllium / Monazite sand / Zirconium / Plutonium (any one)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (a) Uranium, Thorium, Beryllium, Monazite sand, zirconium, plutonium (Any one)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Uranium (also accepted: Thorium, Beryllium, Monazite sand, Zirconium, Plutonium).
common_errors: Some candidates did not mention the radioactive mineral but 'coal' instead.
In some cases, candidates mentioned the 'process of nuclear energy generation'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Help students in building conceptual clarity. Students may be advised to read the question properly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name the non-conventional energy source that has the most widespread potential usage in India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (b) Solar energy
marking_schemes.model_answer: Solar energy
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss advantages of non-conventional energy sources.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name an offshore oil field of India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (c) Mumbai High, Aliabet, Bassein (Any one)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mumbai High (also accepted: Aliabet, Bassein).
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned the 'oil field' that was onshore.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Make students understand the difference between 'onshore and offshore oil field'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Differentiate between Intensive farming and Extensive farming.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Intensive – Multiple crops/ mixed farming/ more per hectare yield/ crop rotation small farms, many crops are grown, manure-fertilizers used, and good seeds are used, labour intensive. Followed in dense population areas. Extensive – Large farms, one or two crops are grown, machines are used, capital intensive. In less populated areas, more total yield, use less labour. (Any two points of difference)
key_points: Intensive farming: small farms, multiple/mixed crops grown, labour-intensive, uses manures/fertilisers and good seeds, practised in densely populated areas, higher yield per hectare
Extensive farming: large farms, one or two crops, machine/capital-intensive, practised in less populated areas, higher total yield but lower per hectare yield, less labour used
marking_schemes.model_answer: Intensive farming is practised on small farms in densely populated areas, involves growing multiple crops with heavy use of labour, fertilisers, and good seeds, resulting in a high yield per hectare. Extensive farming is practised on large farms in less populated areas, involves one or two crops with heavy use of machinery and capital, and while total yield is high, yield per hectare is lower.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain in detail all 'types of farming practices' followed in India.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two problems faced by the Indian farmers.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Subsistence agriculture, poor farmers, illiterate farmers, demand for food crops, challenges posed by globalization/ Seasonal rain/ dependance on rain/ lack of irrigation/ lack of credit/ poor seeds/ small holdings/ soil erosion/ lack of scientific approach/ pest & diseases/ middleman/ lack of storage facility. (Any two points)
key_points: Any one problem from: subsistence agriculture, poverty/poor farmers, illiteracy, dependence on seasonal rain, lack of irrigation, lack of credit, poor seeds, small land holdings, soil erosion, lack of scientific approach, pests and diseases, middlemen exploitation, lack of storage facility, challenges of globalisation
Any second distinct problem from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two major problems faced by Indian farmers are small land holdings that limit mechanisation and productivity, and dependence on monsoon rains due to lack of adequate irrigation, leading to crop failures in drought years.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss problems of Indian farmers in class by providing examples from different areas.

marking_schemes.question_text: Give one advantage of transplantation method of sowing rice.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Surety of crop, healthy crop, economical use of water. More production/ less wastage of seeds/ removal of weeds/ easy to harvest.
key_points: Any one advantage from: surety/certainty of crop, healthier crop, economical use of water, more production, less wastage of seeds, easier removal of weeds, easier to harvest
marking_schemes.model_answer: One advantage of the transplantation method is that it ensures surety of crop with healthier plants and more production, as seedlings are first grown in nurseries and only healthy ones are transplanted, reducing seed wastage.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Focus on sharing methods of sowing rice along with the advantages and disadvantages of each.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is 'Ginning'?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Separating seed from cotton fibre.
key_points: Ginning is the process of separating the seed from the cotton fibre
marking_schemes.model_answer: Ginning is the process of separating the seeds from the cotton fibre after the cotton boll has been harvested.
common_errors: The meaning of the term 'Ginning' was not explained correctly in some cases.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure that the meaning of important terms is grasped well by the students and build the conceptual clarity.

marking_schemes.question_text: Name any two pulses grown in India.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Any two from: Arhar/Tur/Tuar, Gram, Urad, Masoor, Bengal gram/chana, Moong, Chickpea, Soyabean, Lobia, Rajma
marking_schemes.scheme_text: (Arhar / Tur/ Tuar), Gram, Urad, Masoor, Bengal gram, chana, moong, chickpea, soyabean, lobia, rajma. (Any two)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Arhar (Tur) and Gram (any two from: Arhar/Tur/Tuar, Gram, Urad, Masoor, Bengal gram/chana, Moong, Chickpea, Soyabean, Lobia, Rajma).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Conduct regular revisits.

marking_schemes.question_text: What is meant by 'Retting'?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Retting of Jute is a process in which bundles of jute stalks are submerged in gently flowing clean water. It softens the stalk and enables fibres to be extracted and used.
key_points: Retting is the process of submerging bundles of jute stalks in gently flowing clean water
This softens the stalks and enables the fibres to be separated/extracted for use
marking_schemes.model_answer: Retting is the process in which bundles of jute stalks are submerged in gently flowing clean water to soften the stalks, which then enables the fibres to be extracted and used for making jute products.
common_errors: Some candidates were not able to explain the meaning of the term correctly.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Ensure that the meaning of important terms is grasped well by the students and build the conceptual clarity.

marking_schemes.question_text: What kind of soil is required for the cultivation of tea?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Well drained forest soil / Well drained mountain soil / Laterite
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Well drained forest soil/ Well drained mountain soil/ laterite.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Well-drained forest/mountain soil or laterite soil is required for the cultivation of tea.
common_errors: Some candidates had written 'alluvial' which was incorrect.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to prepare table/chart to make concepts easier and clear.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is pruning necessary for tea plant?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: To keep tea bush at low level to facilitate plucking and also to allow new leaves to grow & new shoots for branching laterally.
key_points: Pruning keeps the tea bush at a low level to facilitate easy plucking
It also encourages new leaf growth and new shoots to branch laterally, increasing yield
marking_schemes.model_answer: Pruning is necessary for the tea plant to keep the bush at a low level so that leaves can be easily plucked by workers, and to encourage the growth of new leaves and lateral shoots, thereby increasing the yield of tender leaves.
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned 'rationing' which was incorrect.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss the concept of 'pruning along with its benefits'.

marking_schemes.question_text: How are the industries important for India? (Two points)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Industries help in making India self-reliant, provide employment, make standard of living better, increase national income, earn foreign exchange. Makes products for daily use/ makes goods & equipment used for defence. Counters regional imbalances. Help in progress of nation/ promote balance of trade. (Any two points)
key_points: Any one point from: make India self-reliant, provide employment, improve standard of living, increase national income, earn foreign exchange, produce daily-use/defence goods, counter regional imbalances, promote balance of trade
Any second distinct point from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Industries are important for India because they provide large-scale employment and help make the country self-reliant by producing goods for daily use as well as defence. They also increase national income, earn foreign exchange, and help counter regional imbalances in development.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain in detail the 'need for industrial growth in India'. Guide students to use complete sentences while framing the answers.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the difference between Agro based industry and Forest based industry. Give one example for each type of industry.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Agro – industries depending on agriculture for their raw material. Cotton Textile, sugar, jute, food processing industries, rubber, tea, coffee, edible oil. (any one example). Forest – industries depending on forest for their raw material. Paper, furniture, lac, gum, raisin, pharmaceutical, sports goods. (any one example)
key_points: Agro-based industry: depends on agriculture for raw material — example: cotton textile, sugar, jute, food processing, tea, coffee, rubber, edible oil (any one)
Forest-based industry: depends on forest for raw material — example: paper, furniture, lac, gum, raisin, pharmaceutical, sports goods (any one)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Agro-based industries depend on agriculture for their raw material (e.g., sugar industry uses sugarcane). Forest-based industries depend on forests for their raw material (e.g., paper industry uses wood pulp from trees).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Share 'classification of industries' in detail with examples.

marking_schemes.question_text: What has made Mumbai an important centre for cotton textile production? (Write any two points)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Humid climate, availability of raw material, cheap HEP, cheap labour, port facility, market, plenty of soft water, capital, transport network
key_points: Any one factor from: humid climate (prevents thread breakage), availability of raw cotton, cheap HEP, cheap labour, port facility, large market, plenty of soft water, availability of capital, well-developed transport network
Any second distinct factor from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Mumbai has become an important cotton textile centre due to its humid climate (which prevents thread breakage), availability of raw cotton from the Deccan, cheap hydroelectric power, cheap labour, a well-developed port for export, and access to capital and markets.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss in detail the 'factors for location of industries'. Use maps while sharing the concept 'Location of Industries'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why are the petrochemical products in great demand?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Cheap, cost effective, durable, attractive not dependent on agriculture, economically stable (any one point)
key_points: Any one reason from: cheap/cost effective, durable, attractive, not dependent on agriculture for raw material, economically stable
marking_schemes.model_answer: Petrochemical products are in great demand because they are cheap, cost-effective, and durable. Unlike agro-based products, they are not dependent on agriculture for their raw materials, making their supply more economically stable.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Encourage students to read the question prior to attempting.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two problems faced by the Sugar industry of India.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: seasonal, old machines, power cut. Underutilisation of by-products/ diversion for khandsari, transport bottleneck, RM supply waver, short crushing season, poor cane, rate fixed by govt., strike & lockout.
key_points: Any one problem from: seasonal industry (short crushing season), use of old/outdated machines, power cuts, underutilisation of by-products, diversion of cane for khandsari, transport bottlenecks, fluctuating raw material supply, poor quality cane, government-fixed cane rates, strikes and lockouts
Any second distinct problem from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two problems faced by the sugar industry in India are its seasonal nature — with a short crushing season making mills idle for much of the year — and the use of old, outdated machinery that reduces efficiency and output.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Elaborate on the 'problems of sugar industry of India'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Where is TATA STEEL located?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Jamshedpur in Jharkhand (at the confluence of Subarnarekha and Kharkai rivers)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is located in Tata nagar at Jamshedpur in Jharkhand. Jamshedpur confluence of Subarnarekha & Kharkai
marking_schemes.model_answer: TATA STEEL is located at Jamshedpur (Tata Nagar) in Jharkhand, at the confluence of the Subarnarekha and Kharkai rivers.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Use maps while sharing the concept 'Location of Industries'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is the Silk industry losing the market in recent times?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Competition from synthetic fibres, expensive, competition from other countries. Outdated powerloom/ absence of market/ not as per modern taste/ absence of skilled labour/ no testing & grading.
key_points: Any one reason from: competition from cheap synthetic fibres, silk is expensive, competition from other countries, outdated powerlooms, not aligned with modern tastes, absence of skilled labour, no standardised testing and grading
marking_schemes.model_answer: The Silk industry is losing market share because of intense competition from cheaper synthetic fibres and imports from other countries, combined with outdated machinery, lack of skilled labour, and products that are expensive and not always aligned with modern consumer tastes.
common_errors: Candidates were not able to explain the 'impact of recent changes in market conditions' leading to 'poor performance of silk industry'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Connect students with the 'recent changes taking place in India' in relation to the topics covered.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why is it important to have a well-developed means of transport in India?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: For goods and raw material movement / minimise effect of natural disaster. For industrial growth. / National integration/ for labour movement/ for development of economy/ for reducing regional imbalances/ for urbanisation/ development of agriculture and tourism/ for development of backward areas
key_points: Any one point from: movement of goods and raw materials, minimise effect of natural disasters, industrial growth, national integration, labour movement, economic development, reducing regional imbalances, urbanisation, development of agriculture and tourism, development of backward areas
Any second distinct point from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: A well-developed transport system is important for India to facilitate the movement of goods, raw materials, and labour across the country, supporting industrial growth and economic development. It also promotes national integration, reduces regional imbalances, and helps develop backward areas, agriculture, and tourism.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Relate a well-developed transport network to the growth of industries and economy.

marking_schemes.question_text: 'Though an expensive mode of transport, Airways is gaining popularity in India.' Explain giving two reasons.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Airways are extensively used because: Airways are fastest mode of transport/ useful during natural calamity. Airways are free from geographical contrasts like mountain, rivers, or oceans, for example, northeast region. Saves time/ useful for perishable goods
key_points: Airways are the fastest mode of transport, saving time — also useful during natural calamities for relief operations
Airways are free from geographical barriers such as mountains, rivers, and oceans, making them suitable for remote/difficult terrain like the Northeast
marking_schemes.model_answer: Despite being expensive, airways are gaining popularity in India because they are the fastest mode of transport, saving time, and are extremely useful during natural calamities and for transporting perishable goods. Additionally, they are not hindered by geographical barriers such as mountains, rivers, or oceans, making them ideal for connecting remote regions like the Northeast.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Guide students to provide reasons for a 'particular mode of transport'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why are South Indian rivers not ideal for inland water transport?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Peninsular rivers are not ideal for navigation because the rivers are rain-fed or seasonal, they are shorter flows from uneven terrain, have number of waterfalls, because of competition among airlines price is lower
key_points: South Indian (Peninsular) rivers are rain-fed/seasonal so water level is low outside monsoon
They flow from uneven terrain (hard rock plateau), are shorter, and have numerous waterfalls making navigation impossible
marking_schemes.model_answer: South Indian rivers are not ideal for inland water transport because they are rain-fed and seasonal, resulting in low or no water during dry months. They also flow over hard, uneven terrain with numerous waterfalls and rapids, making continuous navigation impossible.
common_errors: Some candidates related the 'inland water transport to the coastal'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Help students to understand the difference between 'inland' and 'coastal water transport'. Explain the characteristics of the rivers of both north and south India.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two advantages of waterways.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Advantages of waterways are: Cheapest means of transport. Suitable for heavy and bulky goods. Fuel efficient. Eco friendly. Less traffic. Comparatively safe. (Any two)
key_points: Any one advantage from: cheapest means of transport, suitable for heavy/bulky goods, fuel efficient, eco-friendly, less traffic, comparatively safe
Any second distinct advantage from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Waterways are the cheapest means of transport, particularly suitable for carrying heavy and bulky goods over long distances. They are also fuel-efficient and eco-friendly, producing less pollution compared to other modes of transport.
accepted_alternatives: Suitable for heavy and bulky goods
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Share both positive and negative aspects of different modes of transport.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why are roadways considered more important than any other means of transport?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Construction cost is much lower than any other mode. Better connectivity and door to door delivery is possible which makes roadways more important than any other means of transportation. Link between other modes. Flexible usage. For perishable commodities
key_points: Any one reason from: lower construction cost, door-to-door connectivity/delivery, acts as link between other modes of transport, flexible usage, essential for perishable commodities
marking_schemes.model_answer: Roadways are considered most important because they provide door-to-door connectivity — something no other mode of transport can offer — and act as a vital link between other modes such as railways, airports, and ports. They also have lower construction costs and offer flexible usage across varied terrain.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss importance of different modes of transport in tabular form for easy learning.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention two advantages of using railways as means of transport.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Railway serves as the cheapest mode of transport for both freight and passengers over long distances. Promote National integrity. Suitable for long distance/ suitable for bulky goods. Provides employment. Reduce suffering during natural calamity. Movement for defence personnel. Can be constructed in different terrain. (Any two points)
key_points: Any one advantage from: cheapest mode for freight/passengers over long distances, promotes national integrity, suitable for long-distance/bulky goods, provides employment, reduces suffering during natural calamity, movement of defence personnel, can be built across different terrain
Any second distinct advantage from the same list
marking_schemes.model_answer: Railways are the cheapest mode of transport for both freight and passengers over long distances, and they can carry heavy and bulky goods efficiently. They also promote national integration, provide large-scale employment, and can be used to transport defence personnel and relief materials during natural calamities.
accepted_alternatives: Cheapest mode for freight/passengers over long distances
Can be constructed in different terrain
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Share with students that 'no means of transport' is safer than the other. Help them to understand 'advantages and disadvantages' related to 'Safety'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Why should Waste Management be practiced in every school?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: To inculcate the importance of optimum use of resources, to analyse/ understand the disadvantage of waste in living/ non-living/ and on the environment, to learn the importance of 3Rs. (Any two related points.)
key_points: To inculcate the importance of optimum use of resources among students
To understand the disadvantages of waste on living beings, non-living things, and the environment; to learn the importance of the 3Rs (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Waste management should be practiced in every school to inculcate in students the importance of optimum use of resources from an early age. It also helps students understand the harmful effects of waste on the environment and living beings, and teaches them the importance of the 3Rs — Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle.
accepted_alternatives: Inculcate importance of optimum use of resources
Understand disadvantages of waste on environment/living/non-living
common_errors: Majority of candidates mentioned answers that had less relevant portion.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Explain the 'impact of waste accumulation' on the 'environment'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention one advantage and one disadvantage of dumping of waste.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Advantage – saves time, saves labour, requires less/low investment. (Any one point). Disadvantage – Spread of diseases and pollutants foul smell. Spoils scenic beauty/ breeding ground for mosquitoes & rodents. Pollution of water (surface & ground). (Any one point)
key_points: One advantage from: saves time, saves labour, requires low investment
One disadvantage from: spreads diseases and pollutants, foul smell, spoils scenic beauty, breeding ground for mosquitoes and rodents, pollutes surface and groundwater
marking_schemes.model_answer: One advantage of dumping is that it saves time and requires low investment. However, a major disadvantage is that it spreads diseases, creates foul smell, acts as a breeding ground for mosquitoes and rodents, and pollutes surface and groundwater.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discuss 'different methods of waste disposal' with its advantages and disadvantages.

marking_schemes.question_text: How is segregation of the waste helpful?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Segregation leads to better and cleaner waste disposal. It encourages the 3 Rs
key_points: Segregation leads to better and cleaner waste disposal
It encourages the 3Rs (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Segregation of waste is helpful because it leads to better and cleaner waste disposal by separating biodegradable from non-biodegradable waste. It also encourages the practice of the 3Rs — Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle — making waste management more effective.
common_errors: Some candidates mentioned the 'meaning of segregation' instead of its 'advantage'.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Share the meaning, process, advantages, and disadvantages of 'waste disposal methods'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention one way in which we can reuse waste.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: By reusing plastic bottles, cloth bags, converting waste into useful articles by DIY – e.g., of reusing waste.
key_points: Any one example from: reusing plastic bottles, using cloth bags instead of plastic, converting waste into useful articles through DIY/upcycling
marking_schemes.model_answer: One way to reuse waste is by converting used plastic bottles into plant pots or storage containers (DIY/upcycling), or by using cloth bags repeatedly instead of single-use plastic bags.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Focus on discussing the 'reuse of waste'.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention one benefit of Composting.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Benefits of Composting: Compost improves the texture of the soil. It aids plant growth and increases the water holding capacity of the soil. It prevents pollution/ checks soil erosion/ reduces waste accumulation. Enhance soil nutrients. Suppresses plant diseases/ rejuvenates poor soil by adding humus. Converts waste into valuable fertilizer. Reduces waste accumulation. (Any one)
key_points: Any one benefit from: improves soil texture, aids plant growth, increases water holding capacity, prevents pollution, checks soil erosion, reduces waste accumulation, enhances soil nutrients, suppresses plant diseases, rejuvenates poor soil by adding humus, converts waste into valuable fertiliser
marking_schemes.model_answer: One benefit of composting is that it improves soil texture and enhances soil nutrients by adding humus, which aids plant growth and increases the soil's water-holding capacity.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clearly explain the 'concept of 3Rs' with examples.

marking_schemes.question_text: How is recycling of waste helpful? Give an example of recycling of waste.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Recycle of waste is useful for reducing disposal burden and also reducing pressure on useful resources. (e.g., Wastepaper recycled and used to make newsprint.)
key_points: Recycling reduces the disposal burden and decreases pressure on natural/virgin resources
Example: waste paper recycled into newsprint / any other valid example of recycling
marking_schemes.model_answer: Recycling of waste is helpful because it reduces the burden of waste disposal and decreases pressure on natural resources by reusing materials. For example, waste paper can be recycled and used to make newsprint, reducing the need to cut fresh trees.
accepted_alternatives: Scrap metal recycled into new metal products
common_errors: 'Use of recycling waste' (example) was not answered in some cases.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Clearly explain the 'concept of 3Rs' with examples.

marking_schemes.question_text: Mention any one initiative taken by the Government to manage waste.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Check degradation of land/check soil erosion, promote wasteland management, restoration of river water quality programmes, conservation of forests/ wetlands/mangroves, to make laws and acts for environment protection, etc. Provide facilities such as dumping area, incinerators, integrated watershed management, raising awareness of 3Rs, Swachh Bharat Abhiyan. (Any one point)
key_points: Any one government initiative from: Swachh Bharat Abhiyan, laws/acts for environment protection, integrated watershed management, restoration of river water quality programmes, conservation of forests/wetlands/mangroves, provision of dumping areas/incinerators, raising awareness of 3Rs, promoting wasteland management
marking_schemes.model_answer: One initiative taken by the Government to manage waste is the Swachh Bharat Abhiyan (Clean India Mission), which aims to eliminate open defecation, improve solid waste management, and raise awareness about cleanliness and the 3Rs across the country.
accepted_alternatives: Laws and acts for environment protection
Restoration of river water quality programmes
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Discussion on initiatives of government and community for waste management will be useful.
